daily_tip.title: The 24-Hour Impulse Control Rule
daily_tip.summary: Wait 24 hours before making any non-essential purchase over $50.
daily_tip.content: Before making an unplanned purchase over $50, force a mandatory 24-hour cooling period. Studies show that over 65% of impulse purchase urges fade within 24 hours. If you still feel it adds genuine long-term value tomorrow, go ahead — otherwise, transfer that amount directly into your high-yield savings account.

tips.title: Master the 50/30/20 Budgeting Framework
tips.summary: Allocate 50% of income to Needs, 30% to Wants, and 20% to Savings.
tips.content: Divide your net post-tax income into three simple buckets: 50% for mandatory living costs (rent, groceries, utilities), 30% for discretionary personal wants (dining out, entertainment), and 20% dedicated to building wealth and paying down debt.

tips.title: Zero-Based Budgeting Technique
tips.summary: Give every single dollar a job before the month starts.
tips.content: Zero-Based Budgeting means Income minus Expenses equals Zero. Every dollar is assigned to savings, debt payoff, bills, or investments before it arrives in your account, preventing mindless leaking of funds.

tips.title: Automate Your Savings on Payday
tips.summary: Pay yourself first by scheduling automatic transfers the day you get paid.
tips.content: Don't save what is left after spending; spend what is left after saving. Set up recurring automated bank transfers from your checking account to your savings or investment account every payday.

tips.title: Audit Recurring Subscriptions
tips.summary: Cancel unused streaming services and recurring digital memberships.
tips.content: The average adult spends over $219/month on active subscriptions, and over 40% forget about at least one recurring membership. Perform a monthly audit of your bank statement and eliminate forgotten channels.

tips.title: The Power of Dollar-Cost Averaging (DCA)
tips.summary: Invest a fixed amount at regular intervals regardless of market highs or lows.
tips.content: Dollar-cost averaging removes emotional guesswork from investing. By consistently putting $100 or $500 into low-cost index funds every month, you automatically buy more shares when prices drop and fewer when prices rise.

tips.title: Low-Cost Index Funds vs Individual Stocks
tips.summary: Diversify instantly across hundreds of top companies with broad market index funds.
tips.content: Over 90% of active fund managers fail to beat the S&P 500 benchmark over a 15-year horizon. Low expense ratio index funds (like S&P 500 or Total Stock Market funds) provide automatic diversification with low fees.

tips.title: Build a 3-6 Month Emergency Runway
tips.summary: Keep essential living expenses liquid in a high-yield savings account.
tips.content: An emergency fund is your financial shield against job loss, medical expenses, or unexpected car repairs. Calculate your minimum monthly survival budget and build a liquid safety cushion in a High-Yield Savings Account (HYSA).

tips.title: High-Yield Savings Accounts (HYSA) Explained
tips.summary: Earn 4-5% APY on your cash reserves instead of 0.01% at traditional banks.
tips.content: Traditional brick-and-mortar savings accounts pay a meager ~0.01% APY, allowing inflation to erode your cash. FDIC-insured HYSAs offer interest rates up to 500x higher while keeping funds 100% liquid.
